result: Yes — a documented bug involved `DateUtils.truncate()`/`round()`/`ceiling()` (all backed by the internal `modify()` method) and their handling of the `Calendar.SEMI_MONTH` field. Because a semi-month isn't a fixed-length unit (it spans either 13–16 days or 16–18 days depending on the month), the field-rounding logic that worked for regular fields like `MONTH` or `DAY_OF_MONTH` produced incorrect results or exceptions when `SEMI_MONTH` was passed in. The fix added special-case handling for `SEMI_MONTH` in `modify()` so that dates were correctly rounded/truncated to the 1st or 16th of the month rather than relying on the generic field-arithmetic path. I recall this as the specific, well-known quirk associated with `DateUtils` in Commons Lang's history.
